... The matter concerning the Ansar did not stop at this generosity and munificence; it went beyond to ithar (preference). Allah the Exalted then says: ﴿And they prefer [the emigrants] over themselves, even though they themselves were in need﴾ [al-Hashr 59:9]. So jud (generosity) is that you give some of what you have, whereas ithar is that you give all that you have and keep back nothing.

Thus the Ansar used to prefer their emigrant brothers over themselves and would give them what they needed.

The word (khasasah) is derived from (al-khuss), which is a small hut they would build from sticks of firewood. It resembles a house but does not shelter its occupant or protect his family; therefore it is the dwelling of the poor man who cannot afford to build.

So khasasah means extreme poverty. Despite the poverty and need that were upon them, they used to prefer their brothers over themselves. We have said that the Ansar, namely, presented us with a model of giving that has no parallel throughout history.

Then the verses establish this truth: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul—it is those who are the successful﴾ [al-Hashr 59:9]. The successful (al-muflihun) are those whom Allah protects and keeps far from this blameworthy trait. The word shuhh (miserliness) — some say it means bukhl (stinginess), but shuhh is more general and more severe than bukhl, because bukhl arises from it. We say: shahha al-shay' when it became little; and since it has become little, you must guard this little so that it does not come to an end and get exhausted from between your hands.

Thus shuhh enters into your limbs and conduct as bukhl. We may say: shuhh is the disposition of the heart, and bukhl is the disposition of the body (al-qalib).

The word al-muflihun is derived from the farming of the land and extracting its produce; therefore we say in the adhan: "Hasten to al-falah" — that is, the attainment of every good.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 59, verse 19:

His saying, glorified be He: ﴿And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾. There, He commanded taqwa of Allah and the application of His method (manhaj); here, He forbade forgetting Allah. That is to say: when you apply the method of Allah, Allah should never leave your mind, because He is your Lord and your God, the One for whom you work.

We observe here that the noble verse did not say to us, "Do not forget Allah," but rather, ﴿Be not like those who forgot Allah...﴾. It is as though forgetting Allah is something not expected to happen from those who believe.

Forgetting (nisyan) is that you have a piece of information, then you turn away from it through other preoccupations, or you neglect it until you forget it. This is because the mind has a focal point of consciousness (bu'rat al-shu'ur) and a margin of consciousness (hashiyat al-shu'ur). Information enters the focal point of consciousness, and as long as it is in the focal point, you remember it.

When it moves to the margin of consciousness, you forget it and need someone to remind you of it so that you return it to the focal point again. Otherwise, if everything remained in the focal point, a person would never turn his attention to anything else.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Allah has not made for a man two hearts within his body﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4]. And among the blessings of Allah upon you is that you can summon the information from the margin of consciousness whenever you try to remember it.

But how was Allah known to them, and then they forgot His remembrance, may He be exalted? They said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was known to all creation since they were all in the stage of dhurr (atoms/particles of souls), when they were in the loins of their father Adam, peace be upon him, and since Allah took the covenant from them:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified"...﴾ [al-A'raf: 172]. So the Truth, glorified be He, addresses in you this dhurra which He took from your father Adam, because He, glorified be He, is alone capable of that; He addresses the dhurra just as He addressed the earth and just as He addressed the bee.

The Truth, glorified and exalted be He, took this covenant from us so that it would be a proof against us if we neglected His remembrance or forgot it: ﴿lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware"* or say, "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 172-173].

It is as though He, glorified be He, says to you: Beware lest you say this saying, beware lest this heedlessness befall you that makes you forget the remembrance of Allah, because you have no excuse in it, for He, the Exalted, took the covenant from us and then His messengers followed one another and continued to remind us of this covenant.

So when heedlessness occurs in a person, this dhurra performs the role of an immune system: it reminds him and returns him to Allah. They said: this dhurra is the self-reproaching soul (al-nafs al-lawwamah) in a human being. If it weakens and fails to restrain its owner, and he persists in disobedience, society restrains him.

If there is no restraining force in society, and society is also corrupt, we say: heaven intervenes with a new messenger.

Until the message of Muhammad, peace be upon him, came, and Allah made his ummah the best nation brought forth for mankind, because it took up the task of the prophets in commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind; you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110]. Therefore Allah made them witnesses over other nations: ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143].

Thus this ummah has borne the task of the messengers, and we have a guarantee that our society is never devoid of elements of goodness and bearers of the torches of guidance, and however much the truths are obliterated and the picture darkened, there will never be lacking a model of goodness and guidance that brings people back to the right path.

And the meaning of ﴿and He caused them to forget themselves﴾: because they forgot Allah, their gods (their wealth and their children) distracted them from Allah, the worldly life preoccupied them, and heedlessness followed them, so they forgot even themselves; that is, they forgot the source of good for them. It is as though they forgot themselves when they deprived themselves of the source of their good.

A person who is severed from his Lord and Creator lives in distress (dank), however much of the bliss and adornment of this world he attains, while the believer connected to his Lord lives happily even if he cannot find his daily sustenance...

When a person sets his goal, the path becomes easy for him and reaching it becomes simple, and people have not differed in this difference except through the difference of their goals in life. So determining the goal is harder than reaching it...

The true goal is the objective beyond which there is nothing further. If you traced back the goals of the whole world, you would find that they end at the Hereafter, where there is success, victory, and everlasting bliss that does not end.

The Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾. It is said: "fasaqat al-ratbah," meaning the skin separated from the fruit. When the fruit or the unripe date is red, its skin clings to the fruit such that you cannot pull it off.

When the fruit or the date becomes ripe (rutab), its skin darkens and separates from the fruit, such that you can remove it easily.

This is the fasiq who has moved away from the method of Allah; he strips away from it easily and smoothly, because he is not attached to it, and when you move away from the method of Allah, you are not bound to His commands and prohibitions.

This is a rational and natural matter: the two cannot be equal in the affairs of people in this world, so how could they be equal before God, the Wise and Just Judge? Far be it from God, for equating them would be folly in the responsibilities imposed. How can someone who walks through this world with loose hair, running riot as he pleases, be equal to someone who has committed himself to the method of his Lord and Creator?

These two in this world represent Paradise and Hell in the Hereafter. Just as Paradise and Hell are not equal, so too their companions are not equal in this world.

We take this matter as evidence for the existence of Paradise and Hell in the Hereafter. If the people of sin committed their sins, corrupted the earth, harmed the servants and the lands, and then escaped punishment and their affair ended with death, then the advantage would belong to them and the loss to the people of faith and steadfastness. This is an matter that is not valid and that reason does not accept.

Among these people are those who justify to themselves their departure from God's method and say: "Even if there is reward and punishment, we will be burned in the Fire and the story will end." They have overlooked the reality of the Hereafter, that it is an abode of eternity and permanence, whose bliss never perishes and whose punishment never ends.

*"Whenever their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins, so that they may taste the punishment."* [An-Nisa 4:56] Note that when we spoke on this verse and responded to a group of orientalists, seven of them embraced Islam in a single sitting, because they noticed in it an aspect of scientific i'jaz (the miraculous nature of the Qur'an in its scientific statements).

The Qur'an was the first to declare that the skin is the source of sensation and the seat of feeling pain, whereas before that they used to say the brain is responsible for sensation.

The phrase *ashab al-nar* (companions of the Fire) and *ashab al-jannah* (companions of Paradise) indicates companionship, as if there were affection, friendship and association between them. The people of disobedience accompanied the Fire and the people of obedience accompanied Paradise, and each of them became attached to his companion, felt at ease with it, was content with it, and even longs for it. Paradise longs for its people and companions and awaits them, and the Fire likewise blazes and seethes with longing for its people and companions.

As for His saying: *"The companions of Paradise are the ones who triumph"* [59:20], yes, they triumphed with the bliss of Paradise, they triumphed with the pleasure of God, and they were relieved of the fatigue and toil of this world. Their thoughts became what guides their lives; the moment something comes to their minds, they find it before them without effort.
